topics.summary: 必做作业使用 GenAI 前，须向教师核对是否允许及如何报告；课程材料未写禁止不等于获准。
topics.scope: Lund 区分课程考核规则、学生账号指引与职工服务；每项必做作业均须核对教师许可及报告方式。 必做作业使用 GenAI 前，须向教师核对是否允许及如何报告；课程材料未写禁止不等于获准。

claims.text: Lund University's student guidance says students who want to use GenAI for a compulsory assignment or examination must check whether it is permitted and how to report its use; presenting GenAI-generated work as one's own may be treated as cheating.

evidence.quote: If you wish to use GenAI for a compulsory assignment or in an examination, you must always double-check with the teacher whether it is permitted and, if so, how you should report its use. Even if it is not clearly stated in the course materials that GenAI is prohibited, it may still be considered cheating if you make it appear as though you have created something yourself that a GenAI tool has generated for you.
evidence.title: How to use generative AI responsibly

claims.text: Lund University Education Board approved regulatory guidelines for first and second-cycle education (effective 15 August 2026) requiring course syllabi to clearly specify assessed learning outcomes in an AI-available environment, and mandating that any course restrictions or reporting requirements for generative AI be explicitly and consistently communicated to all students.

evidence.quote: Guidelines for Generative AI in Education: The Education Board has approved guidelines for the use of generative AI in first and second-cycle education. This document establishes a framework to ensure transparency, fairness and security in the integration of AI into teaching, learning and assessment. [Guidelines for the use of Generative AI in First and Second-Cycle Education at Lund University (pdf)]
evidence.title: AI at Lund University | Staff Pages
evidence.location: Section: Guidelines for Generative AI in Education

topics.evidenceScope: Lund separates course assessment rules, student account guidance and staff services. Confirm teacher permission and reporting for each compulsory task. For a compulsory assignment, check with the teacher whether GenAI is permitted and how to report it; silence in course materials is not permission.

topics.title: 隐私与数据
topics.statusLabel: 请核对适用范围；复核待完成
topics.summary: 学生指引禁止上传他人作业、敏感个人数据或受版权保护材料，学生登录也不例外；职工 ChatGPT 指引还排除医疗信息。
topics.scope: Lund 区分课程考核规则、学生账号指引与职工服务；每项必做作业均须核对教师许可及报告方式。 学生指引禁止上传他人作业、敏感个人数据或受版权保护材料，学生登录也不例外；职工 ChatGPT 指引还排除医疗信息。

claims.text: Lund University's staff AI page says users may not write or upload sensitive material or sensitive personal data to ChatGPT, and may never upload medical information regardless of confidentiality status.

evidence.quote: You may not write or upload sensitive material or sensitive personal data according to GDPR, such as: health information; ethnic origin; political opinions; religious beliefs; trade union membership; sex life or sexual orientation; biometric or genetic data. You may also never upload medical information regardless of confidentiality status.
evidence.title: AI at Lund University
evidence.location: ChatGPT - What is prohibited to write or upload?

claims.text: Lund University's student guidance says students should primarily use Lund-licensed tools such as Microsoft Copilot Chat and Google Gemini, and must not upload other students' work, sensitive personal data, or copyright-protected material.

evidence.quote: When studying, you should primarily use the tools for which Lund University holds licences. As a student at Lund University, you can use Microsoft Copilot Chat and Google Gemini by logging in with your student account. However, even if you are logged in with your student account, you must never upload, for example, other students' work, sensitive personal data or copyright-protected material - this applies to text as well as images, audio or video.
evidence.title: How to use generative AI responsibly
evidence.location: Protect your privacy and that of others

topics.evidenceScope: Lund separates course assessment rules, student account guidance and staff services. Confirm teacher permission and reporting for each compulsory task. Student guidance prohibits uploading other students’ work, sensitive personal data or protected material, even with a student login; staff ChatGPT guidance also excludes medical information.

claims.text: Lund University's GenAI Q&A says generative AI tools are permissible in education when teachers believe they contribute to or facilitate learning, with teachers responsible for informing students about course or programme rules.

evidence.quote: At Lund University, it is permissible to use generative AI tools in education if you believe they can contribute to or facilitate learning. However, there are some important things to consider. As a teacher, you need to: be able to confirm that students have achieved the program's and course's learning objectives; be aware that sharing students' work with GAI tools is not allowed; ensure that every student has equal access to the GAI tools you recommend; inform students about the risks of sharing personal information or copyrighted material with the tools; inform students about the rules for using GAI tools in the course or program.
evidence.title: Questions and answers on GenAI tools
evidence.location: Questions about rules and guidelines - What are the guidelines at Lund University?

claims.text: Lund University's teacher guidance says teachers should inform students after deciding how GenAI products may be used in teaching and should explain whether and how students can use GenAI products in their work.

evidence.quote: Once you have reviewed learning objectives and made decisions about the use of GenAI products in teaching, you must inform your students. Be clear about whether and, if so, how students can use GenAI products in their work. It is also important to inform students about the consequences of unauthorized use of GenAI products:
evidence.title: Guidance for teachers in five steps

additionalTopics.evidenceScope: Lund separates course assessment rules, student account guidance and staff services. Confirm teacher permission and reporting for each compulsory task. Teacher guidance calls for clear course rules, learning-outcome checks and equal access; it also says students’ work must not be shared with GenAI tools.
